BiblicalUsage: Ka-ah is the sinking of the spirit — to despond, to grow faint, to be cast down. The king of the north is grieved and turns back; the false prophets make the heart of the righteous sad with lies; and the psalmist describes the wicked crouching low to catch the poor and the broken in heart.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God sees the despondent heart and does not despise it. The same Scriptures that name this sinking also show Him lifting the broken — and that is where I look when my own spirit sinks.
